title: Skywest Airlines 1834
summary: SkyWest Airlines Flight 1834, a Metro II on final approach to Salt Lake City, collided at 7,000 ft with a Mooney M20 that had strayed into restricted airspace. The NTSB initially blamed the small aircraft pilots for entering the radar service area, while a subsequent court judgment assigned 51% responsibility to the FAA controller who failed to recognize the collision danger on radar.
probable_cause: The primary cause was the small aircraft pilots wandering into restricted airspace while climbing from Salt Lake City Municipal Airport. Contributing factors included the air traffic controller's failure to notice the Mooney on radar and the lack of a Mode-C transponder on the small aircraft.

events.text: SkyWest Flight 1834 was 30 minutes late from Pocatello on final approach to Runway 34 of Salt Lake City International Airport
Air traffic controller directed SkyWest pilots to turn, unaware of Mooney in restricted airspace
SkyWest aircraft collided with Mooney at approximately 7000 ft altitude above sea level about half a mile above ground level
